speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I'm Dr. Agent. You mentioned chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help me understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and do you experience pain when urinating?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. You are a 40-year-old female with a 5-month history of worsening bladder pain relieved by urination, significant frequency, nocturia, and dyspareunia. Have you noticed any blood in your urine, fever, or back pain?

speaker: Doctor
text: The mention of painful intercourse (dyspareunia) alongside bladder pain and frequency is concerning for Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome, but we must rule out other causes. Has the pain improved immediately after urination, and have you noticed any changes in your urine color or clarity?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Significant for bipolar disorder, currently managed with lithium. Social history: Married and sexually active with her husband. No significant alcohol, tobacco, or recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The history of lithium use is significant, as it can cause polyuria and nocturia; however, your symptoms of pain relieved by voiding and dyspareunia strongly suggest Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome. To confirm this diagnosis and rule out other pathology, I need to evaluate your bladder capacity and look for signs of inflammation.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome.
